key_insight: A hybrid classical–quantum model can improve anomaly detection on scarce, highly imbalanced sequential data by using fewer trainable parameters and a more interpretable architecture.
engineering_relevance: This approach is relevant for real-world monitoring systems like large-scale photovoltaic plants, where rare faults must be detected reliably under limited labeled data and tight energy-efficiency constraints.
method: Two-step hybrid classical–quantum architecture for sequential anomaly detection
Designed for small, unbalanced datasets where anomalies are rare and diverse
Evaluated on a realistic photovoltaic-plant anomaly detection scenario
evidence_signal: The abstract reports competitive prediction accuracy and strong generalization on a realistic large-scale photovoltaic plant use case.
watch_item: Practical deployment still depends on robust validation under scarce-label conditions and on access to stable, scalable quantum hardware.
paper_title: Quantum anomaly detection in real scarce data
